title: Log Trace
summary: Log and trace explorer for JSON lines, logfmt or timestamp-prefixed logs (.jsonl, .ndjson, .log, .txt) merged on time, with span records or trace .json files feeding a waterfall: a query bar (text, field:value, -field:value, /regex/, latency_ms:>=200) with a live count, facets that include on click and exclude on Alt-click, an event-rate histogram stacked by level whose brush narrows everything, a virtualized event table with a detail drawer, the focused event's trace waterfall with its critical path, message patterns, pins and history. Send attaches findings.json and window.jsonl; Export also downloads trace-summary.json. Pick it for any question about what happened in a log window and which trace it belongs to.

query.description: Starting query: free text, field:value, -field:value, /regex/ (case-insensitive unless flagged), quoted "phrases", and numeric field:>=N, field:<N or field:N..M.

timeRange.description: Starting brush, { from, to } as ISO times. Null = all time. Brush the histogram to change it.

facets.description: Columns for the left facet rail (up to 8), top values with counts. Click includes, Alt-click excludes; a column missing from the logs logs a warning.

timeField.description: Time column. Null = auto-detect ts, time, timestamp or @timestamp. A name that is not a column fails the load.

traceField.description: Trace id column. Null = auto-detect trace_id, traceId or trace.

levelField.description: Level column. Null = auto-detect level, severity, lvl or loglevel. Levels are compared in lower case.

bins.description: Histogram bucket unit: auto is the finest of second, minute, hour or day that keeps about 100 buckets over the data; second, minute or hour are exact.

groupBy.description: What the Patterns panel groups by: 'pattern' (messages folded into templates: ids, hex and numbers become placeholders) or any column, such as service or route.

customScript.description: JS run last as (t3template, options) to bolt on controls, panels, buttons and presets. See boltOn.

controls.description: Starting values for bolt-on controls, { controlId: value }, applied when customScript adds them (a saved edit wins).

boltOn.summary: options.customScript runs once as new Function('t3template', 'options', code) after the logs have loaded, the histogram and grid exist and the first view has rendered. Drive the view with setValues({ query, timeRange, include, exclude, pins, columnFilters }), a strict object (one undo step per call, labelled by the second argument). Add controls, panels, toolbar buttons and presets; every control edit is one undo step and re-runs its hooks, and undo, redo and presets restore controls with the view. The query language is the same as the query bar, so a bolt-on writes query text (for example latency_ms:>=200) rather than hooking rows. This is a data template (pipeline 'data'): image, EDL and audio hooks throw. Errors log '[t3template] customScript error: ...' and show in a dismissible banner.
api: addControl({ id, label?, type: 'slider'|'toggle'|'select'|'color'|'text'|'button', min = 0, max = 1, step?, default?, options?: ['a', { value, label }], placeholder?, rows?, panel?: 'Title' | element from addPanel, onChange?(value, t3template), onClick?(t3template) }) -> { id, element, get(), set(value), setLabel(text) }. Values: slider number, toggle boolean, select the option value, color '#rrggbb', text string. No panel = 'Extras'. onChange runs on user edits only, not on load. Every control edit is one undo step.

addPanel(title | { title, open = true, position = 'top' }) -> the panel body element (append your own nodes; the same title returns the same panel). 'top' = first in the inspector below the trace waterfall, above Patterns; 'bottom' = after History, above the composer slot.

addToolbarButton(label, onClick(t3template), { shortcut?: 'shift+r' (any key not in reservedShortcuts), title? }) -> button in the header, left of Send.   refresh() re-renders the view after silent changes to instances.

export() -> Promise<{ files: [{ name, type, size }] }>: the Export button. findings.json { query, timeRange, include, exclude, matchCount, totalCount, topPatterns: [{ pattern, count, firstTs, lastTs }] (top 20), pinned: [{ ts, raw }], window: { lines, total, truncated, cap: 5000 }, columnFilters?, trace?: { traceId, durationMs, criticalPath: [{ service, name, durMs }] } }, window.jsonl (the exact raw lines of the view in time order, at most 5,000) and trace-summary.json (traceId null when no trace is loaded); each is attached to the chat and downloaded. Throws on failure. Send (s) attaches findings.json and window.jsonl only.

getValues() -> { query, timeRange: { from, to } | null (ISO), include: { column: [values] }, exclude: { column: [values] }, pins: [{ ts, raw }], columnFilters: { column: text } (the grid header filters), controls }.   setValues({ query?, timeRange?, include?, exclude?, pins?, columnFilters? }, label?) -> Promise<values>: strict, so unknown keys throw; each key replaces. One undo step.

addPreset(name, { query?, timeRange?, include?, exclude?, pins?, columnFilters?, controls? }) / applyPreset(name): a preset is a whole view plus the bolt-on control values.   on('change', cb(values)) -> off.

instances: { grid (t3kit.datagrid holding every event: grid.raw(i) is the exact line, grid.view() the rows in view), histogram (t3kit.chart, histogram of ts stacked by level), spantree (t3kit.spantree: the focused event's trace), history (t3kit.history) }. Set the view through setValues, not grid.restrict or histogram.set, which the next refresh overwrites.
